text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is among the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
Player(x) ::: x is a tennis player.
FemalePlayerAtRG2022(x) ::: x is a female tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
MalePlayerAtRG2022(x) ::: x is a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
CocoGauff(x) ::: x is Coco Gauff.
RafaelNadal(x) ::: x is Rafael Nadal.
IgaSwiatyk(x) ::: x is Iga Świątek.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If a player is ranked highly, then they are among the most active players.
∀x (LostTo(x, IgaSwiatyk) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek is ranked highly.
∀x (FemalePlayerAtRG2022(x) → LostTo(x, IgaSwiatyk)) ::: All female players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
FemalePlayerAtRG2022(x) ∨ MalePlayerAtRG2022(x) ::: Female or male tennis players at Roland Garros 2022.
∀x (MalePlayerAtRG2022(x) → LostTo(x, RafaelNadal)) ::: All male players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
( (CocoGauff(x) ∧ RankedHighly(x)) ∨ (CocoGauff(x) ∧ LostTo(x, RafaelNadal)) ) → ¬(MalePlayerAtRG2022(x)) ::: If Coco Gauff is ranked highly or lost to Rafael Nadal, then she is not a male player at Roland Garros 2022.

Conclusion:
LostTo(CocoGauff, RafaelNadal)
